firmware.notes: Recovered from the live UI (js/remote_web.js, js/aes/util.js, js/libs/public.js) and cross-checked against the shipped image US_AC10V3.0re_V03.03.16.11_multi_TDE01.bin. This line is the AES session family, unlike the plaintext V15.03.06 line.

identify.notes: adv_hard_ver reads 'V3.0' on this line. Confirm adv_firm_ver against matchPrefix as well: the two V-lines are different firmware generations with different transport, and a wrong choice fails at the first decryption rather than at login.

transport.notes: Getters accept a random cache-buster query which the router ignores. Requests need a Referer of http://<host>/main.html to look like the UI.

login.notes: Success is a 302 to /main.html plus a password=<token> cookie. Only a redirect back to login.html is a rejection.

lockout.notes: Readable without a session. Never spend a user's remaining attempts probing passwords.

crypto.notes: AES-128-CBC with PKCS7 padding, base64 on the wire. The sign value is a fresh 16-character key on every call, so a client must fetch it immediately before each request and decrypt the reply with that same key. Reusing a key from login or from a previous call yields undecryptable garbage that looks like a corrupt response.

envelopes.notes: Authenticated replies are AES-CBC ciphertext; the envelope appears only after decryption. Parse JSON first, then fall back to decrypt-then-parse: a plaintext reply means the endpoint was not encrypted.

fields.name: password
fields.notes: MD5 hex of the plaintext password.

endpoints.evidence: Exercised on an AC10 V3.0 running V03.03.16.11; success is a 302 to main.html plus a 'password' cookie, refusal is a bare number.
endpoints.notes: Bodies are never encrypted. 1 wrong password, 2 wrong user, 3 already signed in, 4 locked. Some builds answer 10-14 for a refusal as well. Do not treat the reply body as a page: a refused login can still return the full main page.

fields.name: sign
fields.notes: 16-character ASCII key, regenerated on every call.

endpoints.evidence: Called before every authenticated request on this firmware.

endpoints.purpose: Lock state and remaining password attempts, readable without a session.
endpoints.evidence: Read before login on an AC10 V3.0 to avoid spending attempts.
endpoints.notes: If leftTimes does not decrease after a refused attempt, the attempt never reached the auth check: suspect a held session slot rather than a wrong password.

endpoints.purpose: Firmware and hardware revision, uptime, LAN identity.
endpoints.evidence: Read on an AC10 V3.0 to record the running firmware string.

endpoints.purpose: Compact system tile state including the remote-admin flag.
endpoints.evidence: Read on an AC10 V3.0 as the confirmation read after a remote-admin write.

fields.name: syspwdflag
fields.notes: 0 means no admin password is set, and remote admin is then refused.

endpoints.evidence: Read, written, and read back on an AC10 V3.0.

fields.name: remoteIp
fields.notes: '0.0.0.0' allows every source address; any other value is a one-address allow-list.

endpoints.evidence: remoteWebEn=1&remoteIp=0.0.0.0&remotePort=5000 accepted with errCode 0; the read reflected the new port.
endpoints.notes: Refused while syspwdflag is 0. This exposes the admin UI to the internet.

sources.notes: Login flow, AES parameters and the remote-admin form contract.
Used to cross-check the UI files; the live device was authoritative where they differed.

sources.ref: Reads and one write round-trip on an AC10 V3.0
sources.notes: Every endpoint in this document was exercised on hardware.

provenance.notes: DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE. Only endpoints actually exercised on this firmware line are listed. The wider AC10 map in the v1.0-fw15.03.06.50 document (WiFi, clients, NAT, VPN, system) very likely exists here too, because the page names and goform handler names are shared across AC10 builds, but it was NOT re-verified on V03.03.16 and is therefore not claimed. A client must probe with a read endpoint before offering a write, and must treat a missing feature as unknown rather than absent.

preAuthProbes.evidence: Documented as plaintext and readable before login in crypto.plaintextPaths; returns lock state without a session.

discovery.notes: getLoginInfo answers plaintext JSON before login, so a client can confirm the device is an AES-family build without spending a password attempt. It does not separate this line from the other AES line; only adv_hard_ver after login does that. The picker in the app is the primary path; this probe is a cross-check.
